Incident Bot: [PAGER] HIGH - Customer-facing errors observed in Console model list and API model status  -- paging eng-sre oncall
Alice (oncall): I'm up. Seeing lots of :warning: alerts from frontend traces. Console shows models in 'stalled' state but API /models returns healthy for same model ids.
Omar: I can help triage. Any recent config toggles?
Priya: Not that I'm aware of. I deployed a small routing fix to canary ~03:12 UTC but that was to routing service (no model state changes).
Alice (oncall): Copy. Starting timeline: first alerts 1763250000, spike ~1763250090. Customer complaints: 3 seats reporting failure to start inference sessions.
Sam: On the logs, I'm seeing 503s from console->controlplane calls: `GET /v1/internal/model_status` returning 504/timeout in console logs but control plane metrics show low latency.
Lena: That smells like a propagation mismatch — console cached state vs control plane realtime. Can you paste sample log lines?
Sam: Pasting snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T03:13:12Z] console service - fetchModelStatus id=mdl_274 status=stalled attempt=1 trace=tx-9a2
[2026-03-15T03:13:12Z] console service - fetchModelStatus id=mdl_274 upstream=/v1/internal/model_status timed_out
[2026-03-15T03:13:13Z] api gateway - /models/mdl_274 200 downstream-ms=28
```
Omar: Interesting — gateway returns 200 to clients but console reports fetch timeout to internal endpoint. Could be an internal L4 routing issue (console hitting wrong dataplane cluster).
Alice (oncall): Checking console->controlplane routing table in k8s. Running `kubectl get svc console-internal -o yaml` and `kubectl get svc controlplane-internal -o endpoints`
Carlos: Also check if feature flag `console_enable_prefetch` was toggled for a subset of hosts. That could change which internal endpoint console calls.
Priya: I just checked flag service: rollout for `console_enable_prefetch` at 03:11 UTC to 10% of hosts (automated experiment).
Lena: Aha. If prefetch flips console to call a new internal endpoint path that was misrouted in the VPC peering, console could see timeouts while the public API (gateway) still serves from a different path.
Sam: I'm seeing that consoles with prefetch set are hitting `internal-prefetch.redwood.svc.cluster.local` and those endpoints show no ready endpoints in DNS from controlplane side.
Alice (oncall): Immediate mitigation: rolling flag rollback to 0% for `console_enable_prefetch`. Priya, can you push rollback and confirm?
Priya: Rolling back now. Command:
```
curl -X POST https://flags.internal/rollout -d '{"flag":"console_enable_prefetch","target_percent":0}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****'
```
Deploy Bot: rollout accepted for console_enable_prefetch -> 0% on 1763250160 by priya
Priya: Rollback done. Monitoring for recovery.
Omar: While that rollbacks, we should collect a timeline for RCA: who changed flag, which hosts were in experiment, which DNS records failed.
Alice (oncall): Agreed. Priya, please attach the rollout id and experiment bucket list.
Priya: Rollout id: r-20260315-83. Buckets affected: us-east-1 consoles 10 hosts (ids: c-101..c-110).
Sam: From the console side, logs show c-104..c-107 saw the timeouts repeatedly.
Carlos: I'm exporting the endpoint discovery logs from kube-proxy on the controlplane nodes for 03:10-03:20 UTC.
Lena: Hypothesis A: flag routed a subset of consoles to a new internal-prefetch service which had missing endpoint records due to kube-proxy race after a canary deployment. Hypothesis B: network ACLs or firewall rules blocked DNS resolution for prefetch host in a subset of AZs.
Alice (oncall): Let's test hypothesis quickly: can someone from eng-infra exec into one affected console pod and curl the prefetch endpoint?
Omar: I can exec into c-105. Running: `kubectl exec -it pod/c-105 -- curl -v http://internal-prefetch.redwood.svc.cluster.local/health`
Omar: Response: `curl: (7) Failed to connect to internal-prefetch.redwood.svc.cluster.local port 80: Connection refused`
Sam: Running `nslookup internal-prefetch.redwood.svc.cluster.local` inside pod shows NXDOMAIN.
Lena: That indicates service discovery failure rather than firewall. Need to check CoreDNS and endpoints controller.
Carlos: I pulled CoreDNS logs — there's a spike of errors from 03:09:50 to 03:13:30: `ERROR: plugin/transfer: failed to tokenize message` on the controlplane cluster. Correlates with our experiment rollout time.
Priya: We rolled out an unrelated DNS config to controlplane at 03:09 (small TTL tune) for canary. Could have caused tokenization errors if the config had a bad entry.
Alice (oncall): Immediate actions summary in-thread: 1) Rolled back console flag (Priya) 2) Removed DNS canary config (Priya) 3) Collected kube-proxy and coredns logs (Carlos) 4) Notified affected customers with temporary workaround (Lena)
Lena: Customer message drafted: "We're investigating a partial console outage affecting model visibility for some users. We're rolling back a recent flag and expect visibility to return within minutes. If you see persistent errors, please DM support." Want to send?
Alice (oncall): Send now. I'll follow up for any escalations.
Incident Bot: Incident status -> mitigated (console flag rollback + DNS config revert) at 1763250200
Omar: Post-mitigation checks: API->models health consistent across regions, console model list restored for all previously affected hosts. I'm running a smoke script against c-101..c-110.
Sam: Smoke results: all 10 hosts now resolve `internal-prefetch` and health endpoints return 200.
Carlos: Pushed the coredns rollback: config reverted at 1763250185, Correlated error rate dropped to baseline by 1763250220.
Priya: Note for RCA: two simultaneous changes (DNS tune + feature flag) created a coupling that wasn't anticipated. Rollout gate didn't consider cross-service DNS schema changes.
Lena: For the RCA thread plan: we need timeline entries (flag rollout id + DNS config commit sha + kube-proxy events + coreDNS logs), root cause hypothesis, and a postmortem action list: safer rollout gating, cross-team preflight checks, and a console fallback to API when internal-prefetch fails.
Alice (oncall): Adding immediate action items: - Add a preflight checklist to require DNS config review for any flag touching internal hostnames - Add an automated canary that validates service discovery after config changes - Add console-level fallback to query primary API if internal-prefetch fails for >3 consecutive calls
Priya: I'll own the DNS preflight and automated canary tasks. Timeline: will have PR with checklist by EOD.
Omar: I'll take ownership of the console fallback behavior and open a ticket with acceptance tests.
Carlos: I'll upload the logs and kube-proxy dumps to the incident folder and add pointer here: https://files.redwood/s/i/incident-1763250000-logs
Alice (oncall): Good. Final note: customers impacted were primarily in us-east-1, ~3 seats reported active errors; no data loss, inference requests still processed via API. Marking incident as "mitigated" and starting RCA doc.
Incident Bot: Incident record updated -> severity: high, impact: partial-availability (console visibility), mitigation: rollback flags + DNS revert, owner: Alice (oncall)
Alice (oncall): Handing off to next oncall @Omar for post-incident RCA work. Oncall shift ends in 20m.
Omar: Taking handoff. I'll run through the logs and assemble a timeline + hypothesis list. Please DM me if you have more notes.
Priya: Adding rollout artifacts and commit SHAs to the RCA doc now.
Sam: I'll follow up with a telemetry check in 1 hour to ensure no regression.
Lena: Adding customer followups and support tickets to the RCA doc.
Alice (oncall): Thanks all. Closing the live thread.
